title: CorsPaint vs. Precision Paint Experts
description: HOA boards and property managers comparing CorsPaint and Precision Paint Experts: what to request on insurance, COIs, scope documents, and scheduling.
heroIntro: For HOA boards, property managers, and commercial owners, the paperwork behind a painting bid matters as much as the paint. Here is what to request.

secondary: hoa painting contractors north central florida
questions: What insurance documents should an HOA request from a painter?
How should commercial painting be scheduled around business hours?

sections.h2: A bid package, not just a price
body: CorsPaint is one of the painting and property-service companies HOA boards, property managers, and business owners in North Central Florida may be comparing. When a board votes on a repaint or a manager signs a work order, they are accountable to owners, tenants, or a parent company. That means the documents behind the bid get scrutinized, and they should.
This page outlines the documentation worth requesting from every contractor and what Precision Paint Experts provides.

A thorough package protects everyone. It gives the board something concrete to compare at the meeting, it gives the manager a file to point to if an owner asks questions later, and it gives the contractor a clear scope to work from. When one bid arrives with half the documents of another, the cheaper number may simply reflect the missing pieces.

sections.h2: Documents to request from every bidder
body: A complete commercial or association bid package usually includes:
bullets: Proof of license, bonding, and general liability coverage
Confirmation of workers' compensation for the people on site
A certificate of insurance naming your entity, issued before work starts
An itemized scope listing buildings, surfaces, exclusions, and products
A written schedule, including any after-hours work

body: Precision Paint Experts is licensed, bonded, and fully insured in Florida, with workers' comp covering every crew member. For HOA, property management, and commercial clients, a certificate of insurance naming your entity is available before mobilization, so your management office can file it before anyone sets up a ladder. We use our own crews and do not subcontract, which keeps the insured parties and the people on site the same.

Our itemized estimate names surfaces included and excluded, prep steps, primer and topcoat products, coat counts, and the schedule, which makes it straightforward to present to a board. See our HOA and property management painting page for how we approach communities, and our article on hiring licensed painters for an HOA for a board-level checklist.

sections.h2: Working around residents and operating hours
body: Commercial work is scheduled around operating hours, including nights and weekends when that keeps a business open or a lobby usable. For apartment and townhome communities, a clear building-by-building sequence helps managers notify residents ahead of time. Our multi-family painting and commercial painting pages describe how we stage larger properties.

A crew lead walks the property, measures, photographs conditions, and takes moisture readings where needed. The written proposal usually follows within one business day of the walkthrough. Put it beside other bids using the document checklist above, and ask each contractor to fill in anything missing before the board votes. Nothing is added to our scope later without written approval.

For multi-building jobs, it also helps to ask how the punch list will be handled. We close each project with a final walkthrough where anything not right is fixed, followed by a punch walk the client signs, so the board or manager has a clear sign-off record.
